summary:
I read the code and ran nothing. It supports the release-transient cause, and I found no other cause; no run has confirmed it yet. The check that failed (Conn::check_held_bound, delay.rs:528-543) runs on every held-bytes sample (held_now, :518-519). Its bound is "64 KB + the acknowledged prefix of the front record not yet released". That bound is only guaranteed at the moment of a write. When the front record is released (harvest, :684-685), released[DOWN] moves on to the next record, so the prefix term falls to that record's prefix, which is 0. The held bytes only fall later, when the pump's down loop hands the record to S (:1748, :1759-1761). If the record is released by the pump's up-loop step (:1814) or by the test thread's current() (delay_tests.rs:2279; delay.rs:1557) after the down loop's last check (:1727), the closing block's sample (:1879) reads held above the bound. Nothing grew in that window. R1's own comment describes this state (:1869-1872). "[1, 0]" means one such down sample and no up sample. The bites build has no feature-gated code on this path, so it can change only timing (load from more tests running in parallel).

The fix: evaluate the same formula at every write, which means inside model_write, the only place the held records grow (both directions). Between writes, add a second check that held never rises above what the latest write left. All changes are #[cfg(test)] code or doc text; no shipped code changes.

The finding's example plant (down_free without released_model) cannot fail G-NC2's own scenario, because S drains at once there. It shows up in the stalled-client test once that test's post-hold write offers a whole record. The predicted failure there is "held <= 64 KB + the front record's acknowledged prefix, at every write", left [1, 0], right [0, 0]. The diff text, three plants, the loop's diagnostic, the list of sentences and the size estimate are in my notes file.
findings: F1 The kept evidence: test name at /home/user/Shamble-Frontlines/.gate/u4r/c62h-bound/merge.log:51. c62h-bound-build.md:430-433 records the assertion at delay_tests.rs:2300 ('held <= 64 KB + the front record's acknowledged prefix', left [1, 0], right [0, 0]). The card's 'delay.rs:528-543' is check_held_bound.

F2 What [1, 0] means: Life.held_over_bound is [u64; 2] indexed by direction, DOWN = 0 and UP = 1 (delay.rs:121-122, :382, :538). So [1, 0] is one call of check_held_bound that found down held above 64 KB + prefix, and none up (this test sends nothing up).

F3 Where the check runs: only from held_now (delay.rs:518-519). held_now is called from poll_read :1522, poll_write after its write :1594, the pump's closing block :1879, and the per-second and run rows :1417 and :1445 (this test calls neither of those two).

F4 The accounting: free_budget = 65,536 - outstanding (tcp_model.rs:2211-2214, :91). down_free = free_budget - released_model (delay.rs:473-477). released_model rises at release (harvest :685) and falls only when S has taken the whole record (:1759-1761). Until its ack arrives, a released record's unacknowledged part is counted twice, which makes down_free conservative.
F5 Held grows only at two places: down at :1574 (then model_write :1592) and up at :806 (then model_write :807). It shrinks only at :1748 and :1503. No other site exists (grep over delay.rs).

F6 Identity in model bytes: H = outstanding + released_model + (snd_una - R), where R is the end of the last released record. Acks and releases leave H unchanged; takes lower it. So the held bytes only fall between writes.

F7 At every write the bound holds by construction: n + 22 <= down_free gives outstanding + released_model <= 65,536. The step to now before each write (poll_write's current() :1557; move_up after step_to :1814-1815) has released every record delivered whole, so H <= 64 KB + prefix, and plaintext held is 22 B per record below that.

F8 The transient, in order: a write; acks free the front record's prefix p and the writer back-fills it (held up to 64 KB + p - 22N); the front record is delivered whole and harvest moves released[DOWN] past it, so the check's prefix falls to 0 (this counter moves first); later the pump's take drains bytes[DOWN] (:1748). Between those two moves held > 64 KB + 0 with nothing grown.

F9 When the test samples it: a release by the pump's own up-loop step (:1813-1814) or by the test thread's current() (snapshot at delay_tests.rs:2279; write_all via delay.rs:1557; the pump runs on a worker, spawned at :944) that lands after the down loop's last check (:1727-1728) leaves the record released and untaken at the closing sample (:1879). R1's comment at :1869-1872 describes this state. poll_write's own sample (:1594) can never trip (F7).

F10 The bites build cannot change the code path. The only cfg(feature) items in crates/net are l2.rs:31 and the wt files. npt-l1's bites feature touches only L1Net's private Model and Bite (l1/src/lib.rs:760-819), never Profile. It can change only timing: 9 more QUIC tests (wt_tests.rs) run in parallel in the same binary (no --test-threads at check.mjs:2057; 160 + 9 = 169 tests).

F11 Why only once: a failing sample needs (i) a loss inside a record that the writer back-fills (P2 has 2 % loss, l1/src/lib.rs:186-188; about 21 % of 12-segment records have one), (ii) that record's release by a step other than the pump's opening step, inside a window of microseconds, and (iii) held still above 64 KB at that moment. That gives about 1 run in 100. One failure in about 97 logs cannot tell the two builds apart.

F12 Any real overflow needs released records that are already acknowledged but not yet taken, at a write, with down_free not subtracting them; the model itself caps outstanding at 64 KB (tcp_model.rs:2217-2224; debug_assert at delay.rs:601). In G-NC2, S is a 1 MiB duplex with a reader draining it (delay_tests.rs:2268-2274), so released records are taken long before their ack. Predicted: the finding's example plant passes G-NC2. The stalled-client test (delay_tests.rs:741-839) is where the plant can bite, but its post-hold write is only 100 B (:780): 64,336 + 100 stays under 64 KB.

F13 Nothing else depends on these counters: held_over_bound and held_beyond_budget are read only by G-NC2. Life is built only by Life::default (delay.rs:1050) and lives inline, not on the heap, so ws_conn_fixed_bytes (309,583) is unchanged. No check.mjs, marks.json or ops text pins the wording. The SERIES.md presence tests (names.rs:143, delay_names.rs:449, socket_tests.rs:390) check names only.

F14 Sentences the fix makes wrong: delay.rs:46-51 (module doc), :372-373 (Life doc), :522-526 (the check's doc); delay_tests.rs:2259-2265 (G-NC2 doc), :2293 (the println) and :2303 (the assert message, the exact sentence the finding names); marks/SERIES.md:613 and :642 (ws_down_held_bytes and ws_up_held_bytes, read at the second's end, with the same two phrases in both rows); .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u3c-plan.md:122-124. docs/ has none. Historical records stay unchanged.
proposal:
THE FIX (test code only; nothing that ships changes)
1. Life (delay.rs:370-384): add held_at_write: [u64; 2] and held_grew: [u64; 2], and reword its doc.
2. Conn::check_held_bound(&mut self) becomes check_held_bound(&mut self, d: usize). The body is unchanged per direction, plus one line: self.life.held_at_write[d] = held. It is called as `#[cfg(test)] self.check_held_bound(dir);` at the end of model_write (delay.rs:598-613). Both growth sites extend bytes[dir] just before calling model_write, under the same lock (:1574 then :1592; :806 then :807). The model has already been stepped to the write's time (:1557; :1814-1815).
3. A new function, Conn::check_held_falls (#[cfg(test)]): on every sample, held_grew[d] += 1 if bytes[d].len() > held_at_write[d]. held_now (:518-519) calls it in place of the old check. This is the recommended between-writes check; it can be dropped for the minimal variant.
4. Tests:
   - G-NC2 (delay_tests.rs:2259-2305): new doc; the println prints writes above the bound and samples above the latest write; the assert message becomes 'held <= 64 KB + the front record's acknowledged prefix, at every write'; add assert_eq!(life.held_grew, [0, 0], "held only falls between writes").
   - a_full_budget_... (delay_tests.rs:776-782): the post-hold write offers [0x82; RECORD_MAX] instead of 100 B and keeps its result in `r`. Then come the two held asserts, then assert!(matches!(r, Poll::Pending)), and one doc sentence is added.
5. Docs: delay.rs:46-51 says the bound holds 'at each write' and that held only falls between writes (so below 64 KB + 16,406 B at every moment). SERIES.md:613 and :642 get the same rewording, twice per row. The u3c-plan.md:122-124 correction is dated 2026-11-17 and names U3C-HELD-1.
The whole diff text is in the notes file, section 2.

THE PLANTS (each is one replacement in a worktree copy, run by name in the bites build through main-run.sh, then restored)
- P1, the finding's example: in down_free, drop `.saturating_sub(self.released_model[DOWN])` (delay.rs:475-476).
  - The stalled-client test must fail with: assertion `left == right` failed: held <= 64 KB + the front record's acknowledged prefix, at every write; left: [1, 0]; right: [0, 0].
  - Why exactly 1: 65,360 B are written in 8 records; S takes 1,024 B; by the end of the hold everything is acknowledged, so the planted room is the full 64 KB and the post-hold write takes 16,384 B, giving 80,720 B against a bound of 65,536 + 0.
  - G-NC2 under P1: predicted PASS. Record the run as evidence of what that scenario cannot reach.
- P2, the old bite: `if held > budget + prefix {` becomes `if held > budget {`. G-NC2 must fail with left [k, 0], k >= 1. That is certain, because the test's loop only ends after a write has left more than 64 KB.
- P3, only with the between-writes check: move the extend at :1574 to after model_write at :1592. The stalled-client test must fail with 'held only falls between writes', left [k, 0], k >= 8.

THE LOOP (first step; the test-engineer owns it)
Run it on HEAD plus a diagnostic patch, D-1, that is never committed. D-1 adds two counters: over-samples that had a released record waiting, and over-samples computed at writes. The cause predicts that every failing iteration has held_over_bound == over_waiting == [k, 0] and over_at_write == [0, 0]. Any at-write over-sample, or any over-sample with no released record waiting, refutes it. To keep the parallel load, the loop must run the whole npt-net lib binary each time, not this test alone.

SIZE
About 130 changed spike lines (+80 -49): delay.rs about -31 +53, delay_tests.rs about -16 +25, SERIES.md -2 +2. Without the between-writes check, about 105. The basis is a line count of the diff text in the notes, section 6.
risks: The cause is shown by reading the code only. The loop may not reproduce a failure at about 1 in 100 per iteration, and a loop of this one test alone would lose the parallel load. If its budget ends with no failure, the confirmation needs either D-1's counters or a deterministic reproduction that needs a new cfg(test) forced-loss hook into TcpModel (not proposed now).

The finding's example plant (P1) is predicted not to fail G-NC2 itself, because S drains at once there. The proof that the check still catches a real overflow therefore rests on changing the stalled-client test's post-hold write to a whole record. If that test's 1.5 s hold ever ended with records not yet acknowledged, P1's count could be smaller (still at least 1 if more than 1,200 B is free); it would be 0, and the plant missed, only if 1,222 B or less were free by then.

Checking only at writes would leave the samples between writes unchecked. Without check_held_falls, the claim that held only falls between writes rests on a grep of the two growth sites, so a future growth site added outside model_write would go unseen. Recommended: keep the between-writes check (about 25 more lines).

Rewording SERIES.md changes bytes that are compiled into three npt-net tests through include_str!. Those tests check names only, so the edit is safe for them. But SERIES.md is shared with other lanes' evidence (C62H-BOUND froze two other rows), so the edit may need clearing by the advisor or Mustafa.

The plant numbers (left [1, 0]; k >= 1; k >= 8) are predictions from reading the code. The plant runs must record what actually happens, and any difference goes back to review rather than being explained away.
open_questions: Keep the between-writes check (check_held_falls and held_grew, recommended because it makes 'held only falls between writes' a counted fact), or keep only the minimal check at every write?
May this change reword the ws_down_held_bytes and ws_up_held_bytes rows of marks/SERIES.md (lines 613 and 642), or are those rows frozen or shared with another lane's evidence?

u3c-plan.md is the approved U3c plan record. Should lines 122-124 be corrected in place with a dated note, or should a correction note be added below them? Separately, line 125's up sentence already lacks the up prefix that delay.rs:49 states, a gap this fix did not cause.

Does the first-step loop run on HEAD plus the diagnostic patch D-1 (which confirms the cause through its counters) or on HEAD alone (which confirms only the rate)? And what iteration budget does the disk floor allow?
